# clickhouse_user (Resource)

Manages one SQL user in `local_directory` access storage. The user name and cluster are immutable. Existing users are never silently replaced: import an existing SQL user explicitly. XML users and replicated access storage are unsupported and require a separate migration.

`roles` owns the exact assigned role membership without `ADMIN OPTION`. `default_roles` is independent: every default must be assigned, and an empty set means `DEFAULT ROLE NONE`. Refresh reads actual membership from `system.role_grants`; `DEFAULT ROLE ALL`, `ALL EXCEPT`, and administrative role options are detected as drift and normalized to the declared explicit sets on apply. Settings profiles and row policies are not managed by this resource.

`grants` owns the complete set of direct database/table privileges, using the same scope and atomic privilege rules as role grants. Omitted or empty `grants` means no direct privileges; apply revokes undeclared direct grants without changing privileges inherited through assigned roles. Direct privileges are active without a default role. Refresh and import read direct grants without changing them; include the imported grants in configuration to retain them on the next apply. Replica differences are detected and reconciled. Column grants, partial revokes, grant options, prefix wildcards, and users sharing their name with a role are rejected before mutation.

An empty `cluster` manages only the connected server; `provider.default_cluster` does not apply. An explicit cluster requires `verify_replicas = true` and `replica_hosts` covering every cluster member. Membership is verified against `system.clusters` before reads or writes. Refresh only reads metadata and checks the supplied password by opening fresh user connections; divergence sets `replicas_in_sync` to false and apply repairs it. An unreachable replica fails verification rather than being considered absent or healthy. Import without a configured password cannot verify the password until configuration supplies one.

Passwords are hashed with SHA-256 before SQL is sent. Passwords remain sensitive values in provider state, so protect the state backend. Authentication checks run against the primary server for local users and every configured replica for clustered users. A failed grant or verification after creation retains resource identity. An uncertain clustered create also retains identity because queued distributed DDL may finish later. Inspect partial state and the recovery plan: failed creations may be marked tainted and require explicit state recovery to avoid replacement.

The provisioning identity requires access to user and role metadata, cluster metadata for clustered resources, user lifecycle permissions, and authority to grant the requested roles and direct privileges. It must not be the application user being managed. Changing a password is immediately effective; coordinate application secret delivery and restart separately. This resource does not provide an overlapping-password rotation window.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "clickhouse_admin_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "service_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

provider "clickhouse" {
  host            = "clickhouse-1.internal"
  port            = 9000
  username        = "provisioner"
  password        = var.clickhouse_admin_password
  verify_replicas = true
  replica_hosts   = ["clickhouse-1.internal", "clickhouse-2.internal"]
}

resource "clickhouse_role" "reader" {
  name    = "service-reader"
  cluster = "main"
  grants = [
    {
      database   = "analytics"
      table      = "*"
      privileges = ["SELECT"]
    },
  ]
}

resource "clickhouse_user" "service" {
  name          = "service-user"
  cluster       = "main"
  password      = var.service_password
  roles         = [clickhouse_role.reader.name]
  default_roles = [clickhouse_role.reader.name]
  grants = [
    {
      database   = "analytics"
      table      = "events"
      privileges = ["INSERT"]
    },
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) SQL user name. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) User password; retained as sensitive state and never sent as plaintext SQL.

### Optional

- `cluster` (String) Explicit SQL ON CLUSTER target. Empty manages the connected server only and ignores provider.default_cluster. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `default_roles` (Set of String) Explicit default roles, each also assigned in roles. Empty means DEFAULT ROLE NONE.
- `grants` (Set of Object) Complete set of direct database/table grants. An empty set grants no direct privileges. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--grants))
- `replicas_in_sync` (Boolean) Desired true. Refresh sets false on metadata or password divergence; apply repairs it. Must not be configured false.
- `roles` (Set of String) Exact assigned roles without ADMIN OPTION; independent from defaults.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import

```shell
terraform import clickhouse_user.service '["main","service-user"]'
terraform import clickhouse_user.local '["","local-reader"]'
```

Supply the desired password in configuration after import. Neither import nor refresh recovers a password from ClickHouse. Remove any XML or startup-script owner through an explicit migration before adopting a user; a startup script can otherwise overwrite the managed account on restart.
